title: Sunday · the Rain, 2013
logline: Sixteenth January. The bay in wet-on-wet, two tiers. The third tier, small: a hand drawing a page of a different, cheaper strip. The Strip About Wage Labor begins in the basement of the Sunday.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the bay in January rain from the bluff, gray-green moss, fog, a smear of rusted tin where the cannery is. Wet-on-wet, the paint allowed to run.

image.prompt: an Oregon bay in January rain from a bluff, wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss and fog with a rust smear where a cannery stands, no figures, no words

panels.name: Bay

panels.composition: Tier 2: the drift log on the beach below, in the rain. Empty. Held.

image.prompt: a bleached drift log on a wet beach in rain, empty, wet-on-wet watercolor, no words

panels.name: Log

panels.composition: Tier 3, short, ink only: a hand at a table drawing a page in a cramped grid — a different strip, stick-simple, a man at a register. A check stub beside it: $40. Four words of caption.
props: a cramped page of another strip
panels.caption: Page one of eighty.

image.prompt: a narrow ink-only tier showing a hand drawing a cramped page of a simple comic about a man at a cash register, a check stub beside it, no watercolor
image.notes: The lower tier is ink, not watercolor. It recurs across 2013's Sundays: the eighty-page strip that earned forty dollars, drawn as Wood drawing it. Letter after: 'Page one of eighty.'

panels.name: Page one

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The Wage Labor strip begins in the Sunday's basement tier. 'Page one of eighty.'
